body.next_step: There is no hub CA: no credential monitor has run under tls: auto here.

findings.title: Host execution policy
findings.message: host execution is explicitly allowed: a run forks a harness beside the control plane
findings.remediation: Set executors.allow_host_process: false unless this hub is single-user

findings.title: Host sandbox
findings.message: 1 project(s) opted out of executors.host_sandbox: their runs on this host are not kept to their own project, and can open, list and write every other project here: /home/demo/projects/todo-api
findings.remediation: Remove a project from executors.host_sandbox.opt_out once its runs work in the host sandbox — grant what they need with executors.host_sandbox.read_only and pass_env — or move it to a container executor

findings.title: Host sandbox
findings.message: every run on this host, administrators' included, since it serves 3 projects (and every person's but an administrator's whatever it serves), runs in the host sandbox (Landlock ABI 4 with private mount, PID and IPC namespaces), but below Landlock ABI 6 a sandboxed run on a hub running as root can still connect to the abstract sockets of the host's daemons, some of which trust a caller for being root
findings.remediation: Run the hub as a non-root user, or on Linux 6.12 or later, whose Landlock scopes abstract sockets

findings.title: Sealing key escrow
findings.message: no escrow of CLOOP_SECRET_KEY is recorded: lose the key and every sealed secret, session and hub CA key is lost with it — no rotation can help, since every key derives from it
findings.remediation: `cloop hub key escrow export --output <file off this host>`, and keep the passphrase apart from the file. After restoring a backup taken before an existing escrow, record it again: `cloop hub key escrow verify <file> --record`

findings.title: Static admin token
findings.message: a static token is still accepted beside single sign-on with an enforced role policy: 55e605a4b7d0 (held by a running hub, and CLOOP_UI_TOKEN in this hub's environment; unused for 5 minute(s), last from 198.51.100.24 at 2026-11-16 02:16Z). Whoever holds it is an administrator outside RBAC, and it never expires
findings.remediation: Retire it — `cloop hub token static retire --reason "single sign-on is live"`, or Settings → Static admin token → Retire — and every member refuses it without a restart; then remove CLOOP_UI_TOKEN / --token from the deployment (in Helm, secrets.uiToken or the key in secrets.existingSecret)

findings.title: Rollback protection of edge-fra-07
findings.message: edge-fra-07 runs dev+g0a796d2.dirty, a build that carries no place on main, so its installer has nothing to order an upgrade by: rollback protection does not cover it, and a forced upgrade could still move it to any older release.
findings.remediation: Its agent cannot carry out an upgrade the hub asks for, so upgrade it once on the device, as root: `cloop upgrade` fetches the latest release (v0.0.7 or later) and verifies its signature, then `cloop executor agent install --upgrade --remote-upgrade` restarts the agent on it and installs the helper the Upgrade button needs. From then on its installer refuses any build earlier than the one it runs.

findings.title: Image provenance
findings.message: cosign is not on this host's PATH, so cloop's own images run unverified, with a warning on every run
findings.remediation: Install cosign on the hub — the published hub image bundles it (https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/system_config/installation/)

findings.title: Image provenance
findings.message: ghcr.io/blechschmidt/cloop-harness:latest on sandbox-eu could not be verified (ghcr.io/blechschmidt/cloop-harness:latest has no registry digest — it was built locally or loaded from a tarball — so no signature can be verified for it); it runs with a warning on the run
findings.remediation: Install cosign on the hub (the published hub image bundles it) and let the hub reach the registry and Sigstore (rekor.sigstore.dev, tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev), or pin executors.container.image by digest; `cloop hub doctor` reports what is missing

findings.title: Git interception proxy
findings.message: disabled while executors that clone the project source, or GitHub grants, are configured, so a sandbox is handed the forge credential and the cloop/ branch rule is enforced only by code the sandbox itself runs
findings.remediation: Set executors.git_proxy.enabled: true with tls: auto and an advertise_url your executors reach (or a cert_file and key_file), so the credential stays on the hub and the branch allowlist is enforced on the push. See docs/git-interception-proxy.md

findings.title: Branch-restricted GitHub grants
findings.message: 1 active grant(s) limit pushes to particular branches, which only the git proxy can enforce, and it is disabled: 1 github_app grant(s) are delivered read-only
findings.remediation: Enable executors.git_proxy so the branch lists are enforced on the push, or re-grant without --branches if an unrestricted push is what was meant. See docs/guides/secrets.md#limiting-pushes-to-particular-branches

findings.title: Kubernetes access monitor
findings.message: disabled; 1 kubeconfig grant(s) are delivered without it on an administrator's acknowledgement, so the sandbox holds the cluster credential and their limits are not enforced: grant_f4b5e9cb7d17599872da8381 to label:region=eu-central (staging-kubeconfig: namespaces todo, web and read-only access (get, list, watch)), acknowledged by dana@demo.example.com on 2026-11-18: "Staging only; the cluster's own RBAC limits cloop-bot to these namespaces."
findings.remediation: Set executors.kube_guard.enabled: true with tls: auto, then withdraw each acknowledgement with `cloop hub grant unguarded <grant-id> --withdraw`

findings.title: Audit head checkpoints
findings.message: every 5m0s, to stderr only: they pin the trail only if a log pipeline ships this hub's stderr off the machine
findings.remediation: Also set audit.checkpoints.file to a path on storage the database does not share, unless this hub's stderr already leaves the machine

findings.title: Audit forwarding
findings.message: no audit sink is configured: the trail's content leaves this hub only when someone runs `cloop audit-log export`, and rows deleted from state.db before then are gone — checkpoints say that they were deleted, not what they said
findings.remediation: Configure audit.forward.sinks (syslog over TLS, an HTTPS collector or Splunk HEC, or a file off this volume); see the runbook's "Forwarding the trail off the box"

findings.title: Quota policy
findings.message: single sign-on is on but no quota bounds anything (ui.quotas sets nothing, or only ceilings that mean unlimited — a negative one, or max_sessions: 0), so every authenticated identity may create unlimited projects and run unlimited concurrent tasks
findings.remediation: Set ui.quotas.defaults (max_projects, max_concurrent_tasks, daily_token_budget are the ones that bound a shared hub)
